clue.text: Winter party cocktail?

parts.note: snow is the weather that defines winter, standing for the season here
a ball is a formal dancing party

explanation.surface: A seasonal celebration with a drinks menu to match.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a cocktail is being built from two loosely clued parts. A Snowball is a British Christmas drink of advocaat and lemonade.
explanation.definitionFit: The question mark admits this is an example: a Snowball is a festive mixed drink made with advocaat.

clue.text: Argentine fossil vertebrae exhibits

indicators.note: exhibits says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A museum label: some fossilised backbones from Argentina are on display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Argentine' looks like a nationality, but it is an old word for the metal (Latin argentum).
explanation.definitionFit: Argentine is an archaic and heraldic term meaning made of or resembling the precious white metal.

clue.text: Her actors retrained as musicians

indicators.note: retrained means the letters of her actors are taught a new order

explanation.surface: A theatre company's cast has been reskilled to play instruments instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A body of instrumental players performing together is collectively a group of musicians.

clue.text: Wolf down starters of beef or lamb tikka

indicators.note: starters, as at a meal, are the opening letters of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Someone gobbling the curry-house menu of beef or lamb dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starters' pretends to be the first course of a meal; it takes the first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To bolt food is to eat it greedily and fast, the same as wolfing it down.

clue.text: Wary about companion's carnality

indicators.note: about means the word for wary is placed around the abbreviation

parts.note: leery means suspicious or wary
CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: Someone suspicious of what their partner gets up to sexually.
explanation.definitionFit: Lechery is excessive sexual desire, so it is a synonym for carnality or lust.

clue.text: Artist penning book with ends of crayons

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the stubs go around the book abbreviation

parts.note: the worn-down ends left of crayons are stubs

explanation.surface: A painter at work with a book and some crayon stumps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends of crayons' reads as a letter-picking instruction, but it means the stubs left over.
explanation.definitionFit: George Stubbs was an eighteenth-century English painter famous for his pictures of horses.

clue.text: Tube employee who operates from home

parts.note: the tube is slang for television, the telly or tele
a worker is an employee

explanation.surface: A London Underground staff member who somehow works remotely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tube' suggests the London Underground; here it is the television.
explanation.definitionFit: A teleworker is someone employed who does their job remotely, typically from their house.

clue.text: Aggressively masculine yet essentially fetching

parts.note: yet and but are both conjunctions of contrast

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence or heart of the word fetching, its middle pair

explanation.surface: Someone tough and macho, but attractive all the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fetching' looks like part of the description (attractive); only its central letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Butch describes an assertively masculine manner or appearance, so it matches aggressively masculine.

clue.text: Hogs peed all over farmer's best friend

indicators.note: all over suggests the letters of hogs peed are spread every which way

explanation.surface: Pigs have urinated everywhere around the farmyard.
explanation.definitionFit: Echoing a dog being man's best friend, the collie that herds the flock is the farmer's faithful helper.

clue.text: Dose of Aspirin, for example, efficient in races

indicators.note: in means the word for efficient sits inside the races abbreviation

parts.note: TT is the Tourist Trophy, the Isle of Man motorcycle races
able means competent or efficient

explanation.surface: A pill that makes you perform well in races, like a doping agent.
explanation.walkthrough: TT is the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy motorcycle races.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspirin is commonly taken as a single pill, a compressed unit of medicine.

clue.text: Pub dashed would-be healthier claim

definitions.meaning: in Britain your ... is the pub nearest your home
with a hyphen the word becomes ..., a label claiming low calories

explanation.surface: A dieter's boast of healthier drinking at the pub, cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dashed' looks like 'thwarted' but means written with a dash, splitting the word into lo-cal, low-calorie.
explanation.definitionFit: A local is a British regular pub; lo-cal is advertising shorthand for low in calories.

clue.text: Mixing hot treacle endlessly makes pudding

indicators.note: mixing stirs the letters about like ingredients into a new order
endlessly means the word treacle loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A cook stirring hot treacle without stopping to make a dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' looks like 'continuously' but drops the last letter of treacle; that and HOT are then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlotte is a baked or set dessert, such as apple charlotte, enclosed in bread or sponge.

clue.text: Paradise in secluded England

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the words secluded England

explanation.surface: A quiet corner of England as heaven on earth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Garden in Genesis is the biblical paradise where Adam and Eve lived.

clue.text: Blokes' joint creates camaraderie

parts.note: blokes are men, or fellows
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: Men sharing a joint (a cannabis cigarette) bonds them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' suggests a shared smoke; it is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Fellowship is friendly companionship among people, the same as comradeship or camaraderie.

clue.text: Socialist woman's circle that is misleading

parts.note: red is a common label for a socialist or communist
her is the possessive for a woman
a ring is a circle

explanation.surface: A left-wing woman's group described as deceptive.
explanation.definitionFit: A red herring is a false clue or distraction, something that leads people astray.

clue.text: Fixed enclosure containing fish

indicators.note: containing means the pig pen holds the fish inside it

parts.note: a sty is a pen or enclosure for pigs
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A permanent pen with a fish inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fixed' looks like an adjective about the enclosure; it is the definition, as in a fixed stare.
explanation.definitionFit: A steely gaze is one that is hard and unwavering, so fixed in the sense of resolute.

clue.text: Rent fuss causes violent storm

parts.note: rent as a past participle means torn
ado means fuss or bother

explanation.surface: An argument over rent payments blows up into a tempest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like money paid to a landlord; it means ripped.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violently rotating column of wind, a destructive kind of storm.

clue.text: Landslide victory gained by one in a Chanel ensemble

indicators.note: in means the joined pair goes inside a followed by the rearranged designer name
ensemble suggests an outfit, but here it means the letters of Chanel put together anew
gained by means the victory abbreviation is taken on by the letter for one, joining it

parts.note: A means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: A sweeping win for a model wearing a Chanel outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Landslide victory' looks like one phrase; 'Landslide' alone is the definition, and 'victory' is just its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An avalanche is a sudden mass fall of snow or rock down a slope, like a landslide.

clue.text: Spots the French going after their neighbour's charcuterie

indicators.note: going after means the French article follows the cured ham

parts.note: speck is a German and Tyrolean cured ham, from a neighbour of France
les is a French word for the

explanation.surface: A French person spotting German cold meats on the counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'their neighbour' refers back to the French: Germany, home of speck, a smoked cured ham.
explanation.definitionFit: Speckles are small marks or flecks, so the word means spots as a plural noun.

clue.text: From beginning to end, pesticide hurts fruit

indicators.note: from beginning to end picks just the first and final letters of pesticide

parts.note: aches means hurts, as a verb

explanation.surface: Chemical spray damaging an orchard crop from start to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From beginning to end' sounds like 'throughout'; it takes only the outer letters of pesticide.
explanation.definitionFit: Peaches are soft, stone fruits with downy skin, a plural example of fruit.

clue.text: Performance about publicity trail

indicators.note: about means the word for performance goes around the publicity word

parts.note: a show is a performance
an ad is publicity, an advertisement

explanation.surface: A theatrical show being promoted through a publicity tour or trailer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trail' looks like a noun as in a trailer; it is the verb, to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: To shadow someone is to follow them secretly, the same as to trail them.

clue.text: Roman leader's vehicle circumvents sinister-looking marine

indicators.note: circumvents means goes around, so the vehicle surrounds the other part

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: sinister is Latin for left, so looking left means read leftwards

parts.note: marine as a noun relates to the sea

explanation.surface: An emperor's chariot dodging a menacing-looking sea creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sinister-looking' seems to mean menacing; in an across clue, looking left reads SEA backwards as ESA.
explanation.definitionFit: Julius Caesar was the Roman general and dictator, and the name became the title of emperors.

clue.text: Clinton's issue with part of London

definitions.meaning: issue means offspring: the only child of Bill and Hillary Clinton
a fashionable district of west London, by the Thames

explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' looks like a political problem; it means a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Chelsea Clinton is the daughter of the former US president, and Chelsea is a district of London.

clue.text: Academic head maintains setter's lower status

indicators.note: maintains means holds, so the dean keeps the pronoun inside

parts.note: a dean is the head of a college or faculty
the setter refers to themselves as me

explanation.surface: A senior academic insists the puzzle-setter is of lowly rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lower status' reads as a noun phrase; it is a verb phrase, to lower someone's status.
explanation.definitionFit: To demean someone is to cause them to lose dignity or respect, degrading their standing.

clue.text: Can reset by scrambling controls electronically

indicators.note: scrambling suggests encryption, but the letters of can reset by are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A tech instruction: resetting a device by encrypting it.
explanation.definitionFit: To cybernate is to control a process automatically by computer, an automation sense.

clue.text: Beauty may have appeal over the phone

indicators.note: over the phone means heard rather than seen, so a word that sounds alike

parts.note: a bell may ring a peal, so the clue's appeal is a pun on that ringing

explanation.surface: An attractive person who sounds alluring when you call them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appeal' must be split as 'a peal': something that may have a peal is a BELL, and BELLE sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A belle is a beautiful woman, especially the most admired one at a gathering.

clue.text: Old president pursues black cutie

indicators.note: pursues means follows, so the president's name comes after the black letter

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
Abe is Abraham Lincoln, a nineteenth-century US president

explanation.surface: A former president chasing an attractive young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Babe is an informal word for an attractive young person, much like cutie.

clue.text: Bring up forecast for fantastic captain

indicators.note: bring up in a down clue means the word is raised, read from bottom to top

parts.note: an omen is a sign that forecasts the future

explanation.surface: Reporting a prediction to a ship's commander from a fantasy tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Nemo commands the submarine Nautilus in Jules Verne's science fiction, a fictional captain.

clue.text: Spooner's parrot cuts back sticky treats

indicators.note: Spooner's signals the opening sounds of the two words are swapped

parts.note: Polly is the traditional name for a pet parrot
lops means cuts back, as in pruning

explanation.surface: A pet bird pecking at and trimming some sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of POLLY LOPS gives LOLLY POPS, spelt as the sweets.
explanation.definitionFit: Lollipops are hard sugary sweets on a stick, a kind of confectionery.

clue.text: Host read out his letters

indicators.note: read out means the two letters are spoken, giving the spelling of how they sound

parts.note: the host's initials are MC, short for master of ceremonies

explanation.surface: A presenter reading out a letter of his on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his letters' looks like correspondence; it means the abbreviation for the host.
explanation.definitionFit: An emcee is a master of ceremonies, the person who presents an event, so a host.

clue.text: Allegedly eliminate means of present transportation?

indicators.note: allegedly means as it is said, so a word with the same spoken sound

parts.note: to slay is to kill or eliminate

explanation.surface: Rumours of a plot to wipe out a modern transport system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like 'current'; it means a gift, as delivered by Father Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Santa Claus delivers gifts in a reindeer-drawn sled, his vehicle for carrying them.

clue.text: Refusal abroad to accept a European emperor

indicators.note: to accept means the refusal takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: non is French for no, a refusal in a foreign tongue
a Pole is a European from Poland

explanation.surface: A foreign refusal to admit a European ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon Bonaparte crowned himself ruler of the French Empire in 1804.
